policy.description: Broken Python→TypeScript auto-conversions under ipfs_accelerate_js/test are intentionally invalid fixtures, not MCP/runtime contract sources.
web/legacy-archive retains intentionally broken and historical front-end sources outside the active contract surface.
docs/ast_exports holds generated AST dumps; oversize or corrupt entries are generated artifacts, not parser defects.
benchmark-results sample files are diagnostic dumps, not contract-bearing sources.
test/web_platform_test_output holds generated run output, not authoritative sources.
test/mocks stubs (excluding MCP surfaces) are intentionally incomplete compatibility shims.
Paths whose basename marks them broken are intentionally invalid fixtures retained for regression.
test/fixed_web_platform retains historical broken Python fixtures.
Sources exceeding the reviewed UTF-8 byte bound are typed as oversized artifacts rather than free-form parse failures.
Files whose contents begin with a non-JS/TS shebang but carry a parser-eligible extension are misclassified extension artifacts.

repairs.description: Collapse volatile TypeScript diagnostic text into a stable ordered set of TSxxxx codes so cluster identity is content-addressed and independent of column drift.

negative_fixtures.notes: Unterminated string remains a typed parse failure.

positive_fixtures.notes: Valid TS source must not enter a failure cluster.

repairs.description: Detect bash/python shebang bodies under .js/.ts extensions and reclassify them as unsupported/misclassified rather than silent success or untyped failure.

negative_fixtures.notes: Bash shebang under .js must not be labeled success.

positive_fixtures.notes: Real JS modules remain parser-eligible successes.

repairs.description: MCP/runtime contract surfaces remain in the failure budget even when surrounding test trees are excluded by reviewed policy.

negative_fixtures.notes: mockMCPClient syntax errors must remain budgeted failures.

positive_fixtures.notes: Non-MCP test fixtures may be excluded by policy.
